rules.title: Visual Hierarchy
rules.description: The first screen has a clear focal point. Objective check (the supported part): weigh each first-screen element by visible area and contrast (filled buttons count extra, images count 0.6) and require the headline and the main action together to hold at least 25% of the total. A person judges whether the focal point is the right one.
rules.source: Refactoring UI, labels are a last resort
rules.evaluationPrompt: Evaluate ONLY this rule: "Visual Hierarchy". Identify the element attracting emphasis and the intended priority. Use only the supplied page context. Quote the exact words or elements you rely on. If the context is not enough to decide, answer "inconclusive". If the rule does not apply to this page, answer "not_applicable".
rules.recommendationTemplate: Make the headline and the main action the heaviest things in the first screen: shrink or move the dominant element, or enlarge the headline. {{observation}} Evidence: {{evidence}}
requiredEvidence: the four heaviest first-screen elements with their weights
rules.userImpact: When the eye lands somewhere other than the headline or the action, visitors may not read the offer or see what to do. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.
rules.businessImpact: A first screen without a clear focal point can lower the share of visitors who start the main action. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.

rules.title: Spacing Rhythm
rules.description: Spacing follows a scale. Objective check: collect the vertical gaps between stacked blocks; flag when fewer than half sit on a 4px grid and 10 or more different sizes are used. Always "needs a person".
rules.evaluationPrompt: Evaluate ONLY this rule: "Spacing Rhythm". Compare equivalent groups and identify spacing that implies an incorrect relationship. Use only the supplied page context. Quote the exact words or elements you rely on. If the context is not enough to decide, answer "inconclusive". If the rule does not apply to this page, answer "not_applicable".
rules.recommendationTemplate: Pick a spacing scale (for example 8, 16, 24, 32, 48) and use only those gaps. {{observation}} Evidence: {{evidence}}
requiredEvidence: most common gap sizes with counts
rules.userImpact: Uneven spacing makes related things look unrelated and the page harder to scan. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.
rules.businessImpact: Inconsistent spacing reads as unfinished, which lowers trust in the product. This is a hypothesis from reading the page, not measured behaviour.
